description:
FILED s473t6b (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 round 9.

The postfix GLOB-SLOT dereference `$globref->*{NAME}` â the postfix spelling
of `*foo{NAME}` â is a #138 DROP.  Every OTHER postfix-deref spelling works;
this is the one hole, measured spelling by spelling (probes/p12.pl):

    ->@*   ->%*   ->$*   ->$#*   ->@[..]   ->@{..}   ->**   'name'->**   all OK
    ->*{CODE}  ->*{ARRAY}  ->*{IO}  ->*{FORMAT}                      DROPPED

    PCL: statement dropped: defined($gr->*{"CODE"}) â¦
         -- PExpr: unhandled postfix '->' term in (unknown):
            term='Token::Operator<->>' next='Token::Cast<*>'
            next2='Structure::Subscript<{"CODE"}>'

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    our @a = (1,2,3); sub c { 7 }
    my $gr = \*main::a;
    printf "%s\n", ref($gr->*{ARRAY});      # perl: ARRAY   PCL: dropped
    printf "%s\n", (defined($gr->*{CODE}) ? "y" : "n");  # perl: n

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/postfixderef.t 27 `glob access
syntax` (the file's `ok(eval q{'mysubalias'->** = 'mysub'->**->*{CODE}})`,
which is the drop inside a string eval, so it DIES â #363 â and the row fails
rather than the file aborting), and 73 `IO slot of the temporary glob is set
correctly`.  op/ref.t's `ref to format` row is the same slot family.

SHAPE: one arm in PExpr's postfix `->` term walker, for `Token::Cast<*>`
followed by a `Structure::Subscript`.  The VALUE it must produce is #1664's
typeglob model (a slot accessor answering a ref of the right kind, or undef
for an empty slot â and undef for CODE on a glob with no sub, which is the
row above), so the parse arm is cheap and the semantics come from #1664.  Do
NOT add it as a synonym for `->**`: `->*{NAME}` selects ONE slot and answers
undef when it is empty, where `->**` is the glob itself.


=== NEIGHBOUR FINDING (s491, Fable, 2026-09-19; main 4c6565e5; pre-existing) ===
A SLICE followed by a postfix deref SILENTLY DROPS the deref: `my @nest = ([1,2],[3,4,5]); join ",", @nest[1]->@*` is `3,4,5` in perl (the slice`s LAST element, dereferenced) and `ARRAY(0x1)` in PCL; `@nest[0,1]->@*` -> perl `3,4,5`, PCL `ARRAY(0x2),ARRAY(0x1)`.  `$nest[1]->@*` and `(@nest[1])[0]->@*` are right.  Rare spelling (perl warns "better written as $nest[1]"), but it is a SILENT wrong, so rule 12 says the term walker should either lower it or DIE naming it.  Probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/p-slice-postfix.pl.  Round t6d owns op/postfixderef.t and should check whether any of its rows is this shape.
subject: postfix glob-slot deref $gr->*{NAME} is a #138 DROP -- the one postfix-deref spelling PExpr has no arm for
